title: Haitian Third-Grader Taken Into Federal Custody After San Diego ICE Check-In
excerpt: San Diego Unified says an 8-year-old Fay Elementary student was separated from the uncle caring for him at a scheduled appointment. DHS says the man could not establish legal guardianship, so the boy was classed as an unaccompanied minor and sent to the Office of Refugee Resettlement.
body:
• An 8-year-old Haitian third-grader at Fay Elementary School in San Diego was taken into federal custody after his uncle brought him to a scheduled ICE check-in. His school district says it does not know which federal facility is holding him.
  • The Department of Homeland Security says the man who brought the boy could not establish legal guardianship, so ICE classified him as an unaccompanied minor and placed him with the Office of Refugee Resettlement.
  • The boy previously held Temporary Protected Status. Haiti's TPS designation ended on July 27, 2026, and USCIS says employment authorization documents in categories A12 and C19 issued under Haiti TPS are no longer valid.
  • San Diego Unified has sent crisis counselors to Fay Elementary and, with city and union leaders, has demanded that federal agencies keep children in custody close to their home schools.

An 8-year-old Haitian boy who attends third grade at Fay Elementary School in San Diego's City Heights neighborhood was taken into federal custody after he arrived for a scheduled immigration check-in with the uncle who has cared for him since his father was deported. Video recorded by a volunteer observer at the ICE field office in downtown San Diego shows officers leading the boy away, according to NBC News, and as of Monday his family did not know exactly where he was being held.

What happened at the check-in

According to a letter San Diego Unified School District officials sent on November 6 to Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin and Health and Human Services Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr., the child received a letter summoning him to meet an ICE agent. His uncle took him to the appointment, the district wrote, "because he did not want to break the law." The district says the agent then used the William Wilberforce Trafficking Victims Protection Reauthorization Act of 2008 to take the child into custody, "leaving the uncle distraught, and this eight-year-old without the support of their family, community and their school." District spokesperson James Canning told the USA TODAY Network that officials believe it occurred on November 4. The district has not released the boy's name and does not know what facility he was placed in.

Guerline Jozef, executive director of the Haitian Bridge Alliance, said in a statement reported by NBC News that even though the uncle followed the rules, "the child was taken into custody and subsequently transferred to the Office of Refugee Resettlement," the HHS agency that takes custody of children deemed to be unaccompanied minors. Rep. Juan Vargas's office is handling the family's casework, NBC News reported.

The government's account

DHS disputes the district's framing. A spokesperson told the USA TODAY Network that a man "claiming to be the child's uncle took him to an ICE check-in," that ICE confirmed he was not part of either family unit the child had lived with, and that it occurred on November 5. Because he could not establish legal guardianship, the boy was determined to be an unaccompanied minor.

https://x.com/ICEgov/status/2106553693042618668

"Out of an abundance of caution and to ensure the child's safety, ICE determined it was best to remove the child from the household and place him in the care of the Office of Refugee Resettlement."

— Department of Homeland Security spokesperson, in a statement to USA TODAY

DHS also said allegations that ICE took a third grader into custody to place him in detention are "false," and that the boy was brought into the United States by a man who alleged to be his father, who was previously removed to Mexico by Customs and Border Protection. The Office of Refugee Resettlement told NBC News it does not comment on specific cases, citing privacy policies for children in its custody.

How a check-in becomes an unaccompanied-minor case

Under the 2008 trafficking law, a child under 18 who has no legal immigration status and no parent or legal guardian available to care for them is treated as an unaccompanied minor. Immigration authorities generally have 72 hours to hand such children to ORR, which shelters them until it can vet a parent or relative to take them in, according to USA TODAY's reporting. As of November 5, 1,620 children were in HHS custody as unaccompanied minors, according to agency data cited by USA TODAY. Relatives can apply to receive a child from ORR, but advocates say tighter sponsor requirements have made that harder and lengthened shelter stays.

https://www.instagram.com/p/DfhSlNal9nL/

Why TPS is at the center of this case

School officials wrote that the boy previously had Temporary Protected Status, first granted to Haitians after the 2010 earthquake, which shielded beneficiaries from deportation and allowed them to live and work in the United States. The Trump administration argued Haiti no longer met the conditions for it. After the Supreme Court cleared the way in June 2026, TPS for Haitians ended on July 27, 2026, according to USCIS. For diaspora families, the consequence is direct: status and work authorization tied solely to Haiti TPS no longer apply, and an immigration appointment now carries custody risk for children whose caregivers cannot document legal guardianship.

What the district is demanding

San Diego Unified's superintendent and board president signed the November 6 letter alongside a city councilmember and leaders of unions representing education workers. They asked HHS and ORR to keep children in custody as close as possible to their home schools, to work with school districts before relocation decisions are finalized, and to track educational outcomes for affected children. "Every child deserves stability, dignity, and access to education," they wrote, in the letter reported by USA TODAY. HHS and ORR did not immediately respond to the demands, and the boy's exact placement remains undisclosed.
nri_angle: The case shows how the end of Haiti TPS on July 27, 2026 reaches into US classrooms: a child who complied with an ICE summons was reclassified as an unaccompanied minor because his caregiver could not document legal guardianship.
